body:
**What breaks:** on the retired Windows runner (its code out of the tree, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) a key written into ConPTY right after `ResizePseudoConsole` returned was never read by the Rust test child, which was blocked in its console read (`ReadConsoleW` through Rust's stdin): measured 13 losses in 200 isolated iterations (6.5 %) of `spawn_runs_a_raw_child_that_sees_its_size_a_resize_and_its_own_exit_code` under `cargo llvm-cov nextest` on `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260922.246.2 (ci#36527891850, job 109274838484). Every loss was class K: the child's size watcher saw the new size with no key, viola's writer had written and flushed the key, and ConPTY wrote no cursor-position request (`dsr-cpr 0`). The loss lies between the ConPTY input-pipe write and that test child's read; **where inside that span, and why, is not established** — an overseer read of microsoft/terminal's current source (relayed at the wrap, not verified here) found no input-buffer flush on the resize path and no reported resize input loss, so this is not recorded as a ConPTY defect. This host's conhost 10.0.26100.8875 read 20/20. [retired 2026-11-08, census C-560 of doc:viola-0.2.0/census: a Windows measurement, history; the product window and the test rule below stand]
**The product window — read on Linux for `claude`:** viola forwards resizes and keys as they come and never holds, queues or reorders a human key behind a resize (a11y-plan §1), so nothing in viola closes this window. Whether the real `claude` (Node/libuv, reading with `ReadConsoleInputW`) loses a key typed right after a resize in `viola run` is **unmeasured**; the rate above is the Rust test child's. On Linux the real `claude` on Linux, run unwrapped in the live rig's own pty (its `KR` arm) on two versions, read `kr-reading: kept`: no key typed right after a resize at the delays the arm measures was lost — no loss at those delays on those versions, never «never loses»; the reading is of the CLI unwrapped, not of viola's own poll lag or the driver's paste, so viola adds no wait (route entry «Key after a resize», 0.2.0, Epoch 4; its chunk's `evidence/live-round.md`). The founder's product question on H2 reads answered on Linux by that reading; the Windows window above left the tree with its code.
**How to avoid (tests only):** a test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first — the red test now waits for its watcher's `size 120x40` line, and read 200/200 under the same loop (ci#36529038462). That reshaped test does NOT cover the product window: it proves the key arrives once the resize has landed, not that a key racing a resize arrives, and it reads with the Rust child, never `claude`.
**Fix if broken:** read the kept reports in `<temp dir>/viola-pty-watch/` (`<test>.<pid>.report`, `<test>.<pid>.test.report`, `<pid>` the test process's id) by the chunk's localisation rule — class R (no `size` line), K (size seen, key flushed, key lost) or E (key before size) — before changing any wait; never raise `CHILD_WITHIN` or retry the test.
**With the sideloaded ConPTY** (removed with the Windows code, recoverable at the tag `multi-os-final`) (chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty`, one windows-2025 run, image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260828.587, ci#36563868040, the measurement-only race): sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe` 1.24.260710001 lost 0 of 200, the inbox ConPTY 14 of 200 — no rate claimed, and the product window above stays unmeasured for `claude`. [retired 2026-11-08, census C-563 of doc:viola-0.2.0/census: history]
**References:** arch [PTY]; test-plan §5 Module ↔ PTY, §10 Zero-flakiness budget; chunk `2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe` `evidence/h2-reproduction.md`; chunk `2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty` `evidence/h2-with-without.md`; microsoft/terminal PR #19535 (post-resize CPR — not seen on either build).

- Key after a resize: the real `claude` on Linux, run unwrapped in the live rig's own pty (its `KR` arm) on two versions, read `kr-reading: kept`: no key typed right after a resize at the delays the arm measures was lost — no loss at those delays on those versions, never «never loses»; the reading is of the CLI unwrapped, not of viola's own poll lag or the driver's paste; viola adds no wait (route entry «Key after a resize», 0.2.0, Epoch 4).

- NEVER `sleep` for synchronization — wait on an `events.ndjson` byte offset, `viola wait --after` or a status field; a test that writes a key after a resize sends it only once the child reports the new size, the live rig's `KR` arm alone typing its key right after a resize of its own pty, since that is what it measures. nextest `retries = 0`; no `#[ignore]` as a parking place.

The session measured whether real claude on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize of its pty, and found no loss: claude 2.1.330 (KR) and 2.1.328 (KR8-2) each kept 12 of 12 keys typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after a resize, said as no loss in 12 rounds at these delays on these versions, never as never loses.
No product change followed: the fix half was not needed, no viola-pty, wrapper, passthrough or fake-agent code moved; only the test-only live-round rig changed.
The rig gained a KR live arm (labels KR, KR-2, KR8, KR8-2) that resizes its own pty and types x then DEL into claude's input box, reading the box row's cell attributes only, never text, under a new resize grant word beside box.
The rig's after-key settle was mended for KR alone (quiet counted from a mark taken after the key), telling a late redraw from a dirty box; the shared settle every other arm and the boundary checks use is unchanged, and HB and the earlier arms read as before.
The rehearse verb gained two rehearse-only options for kr (a quiet window of 100 to 400 ms and a withheld or late DEL seam) that the live verb refuses as usage, exit 2; five KR rehearsals over the fake agent were added inside the existing integration suite.
The live KR reading is recorded evidence for the key-after-a-resize item and gates nothing; CI on the pre-CI commit was green 7 of 7.

body: decision/no-screen-content-parsing: its except list gains the KR arm, which reads claude's box row by cell attributes after each resize and key, never text.

decision/boundary-check-never-inspects-claude-content: the new KR arm drives real claude and reads only the box row's attributes and closed words, counts, delays and settle times; a row naming which arms read attributes now has one more.
decision/live-readings-never-gate: the KR and KR8-2 live readings (kept 12 of 12) are recorded evidence only and gate no build; the KR rehearsals over the fake agent are what CI runs.

contract/tui-passthrough/focus-mouse-resize-sequences: the measurement bears on keys typed right after a resize; claude itself kept every key at 0, 20 and 100 ms, so viola's resize handling needs no wait of its own and the contract stands unchanged, now with a Linux reading beside it.

contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes and decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked: a human key typed right after a resize was measured kept on Linux at the CLI unwrapped; no product change, the measurement is not of viola's own poll lag or the driver's paste.

decision/wheel-ignores-terminal-events and decision/non-editing-sequences: resize is the terminal event the KR arm exercises before each key; neither rule changed, the arm only measures the child's keeping of the key after it.

decision/tui-boundary-driver-pin and decision/tui-boundary-assertions-only: the boundary driver (the live-round rig) gained a resize action, a KR-only settle and the KR arm; the pin and the boundary-only scope stand.
decision/a11y-runs-in-existing-test-suites and decision/a11y-inside-existing-suites: the five KR rehearsals were added inside the existing integration suite, no separate driver or suite.

decision/zero-flakiness: the KR rehearsal that ran 12.4 s against its 15 s deadline now runs about 5.1 s under a 100 ms quiet window; the watched rehearsal red of the box read empty after x and DEL stayed green in 4 runs, a hypothesis that it shares the mended settle named on its carry, its rule unchanged.
decision/wrapped-tui-reads-as-unwrapped: the measurement was of claude unwrapped, giving the unwrapped baseline a wrapped run is read against for a key after a resize.

body:
The session measured whether real claude on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize of its own pty, and found no loss: 2.1.330 and 2.1.328 each kept 12 of 12 keys typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after a resize, the CLI read unwrapped.
It added a KR arm to the test-only live rig (labels KR, KR-2, KR8, KR8-2) that resizes its own pty, types up to 13 x and 13 DEL, and reads its box row's cell attributes, never text.
It mended the rig's settle for KR alone: quiet counted from a byte drained after the key, a late redraw told apart from a dirty box, under a rehearse-only quiet window of 100 to 400 ms and a rehearse-only KR seam that a live start refuses with exit 2.
The KR summary and ledger hold closed words, counts, delays and settle times only; the kept frames stay owner-only under the gitignored rig output directory and are never read into evidence.
No product crate, no viola-pty file, no fake-agent file, no log line, no event, no detail code, no config key and no env var changed; the fix half was not needed.

body_fields.what: the test-only live rig's arms, session pump, settle and summary tally — the standing live rig that drives a real or fake claude in its own pty, outside every product process role
the test-only live rig's key grant — which keys and actions a start may type into its own pty
the test-only live rig's screen model of the child's pty, read by cell attributes for the box row
the test-only live rig binary — its live, rehearse and census verbs and their usage refusals
the rig rehearsals — integration tests that run the live rig over the fake agent

body: Typed keys never logged and never in telemetry: the KR arm types x and DEL into its own pty; its summary and ledger record only key counts (keys x 13, del 13) and closed words, never a key stream, in the test-only rig, not in any product log.

No telemetry from screen content: the KR arm reads its box row's cell attributes after a resize and writes closed words (clean, late-redraw, dirty) and counts, never screen text, into the rig's summary, which is no product telemetry.

PTY byte stream never logged: the kept KR frames are written owner-only under the gitignored rig output directory and never copied into evidence, a message or the tree; the rig's settle reads the pty byte stream only to time quiet.
Real-CLI verify never in CI and CI verify against the fake agent only: the live KR start is refused under CI; CI runs only the five KR rehearsals over the fake agent.
Local run outputs never uploaded and the secret-scan scope: the rig's out dirs and kept frames are local, gitignored outputs that no CI upload carries.

No sleep-based log waits: the rig's KR settle waits on a quiet window of pty bytes counted from a mark after the key (100 to 400 ms, default 400), not on any log line; check that no row reads this as a log wait.
No retry policies and no retry-once: the spare start KR8-2 after the cut KR8 is one operator-granted start under a cap, not a retry policy in product code; check that no row reads it as one.
Env names only, never values: the session printed no env value and added no env var; the rig's options are rehearse-only flags.
Fixtures not a telemetry source: the rig's ledger lines and summaries are test evidence of closed words, counts and settle times, not a source of product telemetry.
Every process-log, detail-file, event-stream and diag-line contract (fields, event enum, detail codes, exit codes, corr and conn): no product process writes a new or changed line.
Span and trace coverage, span attributes and span naming: no span was declared, renamed or removed.
The PTY seam log events, the paste log event and the paste write's time bound: no PTY seam or paste code changed; the paste bound is a route entry for a later chunk.
Metric coverage, SLO invariants, hook and perf budgets, heartbeat thresholds and the panic and schema CI gates: no budget, threshold or gate moved.
Error capture and reporting, panic capture by role, redaction, veil and the allow-list: no product error path or redaction changed.
MCP, channel, hook, send, wait, dialog and wheel telemetry: none of those paths changed.
Service identity, config.json keys, diagnostics file locations and modes, and the logging stack: unchanged.

body:
The session measured whether real claude on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize of its own pty, with no product change: the live-round rig gained a KR arm (labels KR, KR-2, KR8, KR8-2) that resizes only its own pty and types up to 13 x and 13 DEL under the grant box,resize.
On real claude 2.1.330 (KR) and 2.1.328 (the spare KR8-2) every one of 12 keys typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after a resize was kept; KR8 was cut at round 8 as unverified by the rig's own settle, which this session mended for KR alone (a byte drained before the key never settles it); no start read lost, so the driver-paste fix was not needed.
The KR arm reads its box row's cell attributes only, never text, and its summary and ledger hold closed words, counts, delays and settle times; kept frames stay 0600 under the gitignored rig output dir; the arm is refused under CI.
The rig's rehearse verb gained two rehearse-only options for the kr arm, --quiet-ms (100 to 400) and --kr-del-seam withheld or late; any other arm or form, and any live start carrying one, is refused usage with exit 2 before any ledger line.
The operator's wrap answers: the live rig's kept-stamp row states its rule and names no labels; the cross-session fixture's runtime-dir path is an accepted residual with its own security-plan row; the four short except cells stand; a route entry for a bounded paste write follows this chunk.

body_fields.what: the live-round rig itself, test-only: its arms (HB, KR and the earlier ones), its grants, its settle, its summary and ledger of closed words and counts
the live-round rig's key grants, which say what keys the rig may type into its own pty and now whether it may resize that pty
the live-round rig's screen model, which reads its own pty's box row by cell attributes and now follows a resize
the live-round rig's command line, its live and rehearse verbs, their grants, caps and refused usage
the live rig's rehearsals over the fake agent, which hold each arm's reading and its teardown before any live start

decision/live-rig-hb-arm-keeps-attributes-only: the KR arm, like HB, keeps cell attributes and counts only, plus delays and settle times; its own row stands beside this one.
decision/live-rig-kept-stamp-owner-only: on the operator's word the row states the owner-only seeded-stamp rule and names no arm labels; the stamp read unmoved before and after KR8-2.

decision/live-rig-isolated-child, decision/live-rig-credentials-copy and decision/live-rig-seed-from-bundle-logic: the KR starts ran the same isolated child with a seeded config and a transient credentials copy; hygiene read clean with 0 host paths kept.

The live rig's quiet and kr seam options are accepted by the rehearse verb with the kr arm alone; any other arm, any value outside the closed form, or any live start carrying one is refused usage, exit 2, before any ledger line.
The cross-session fixture's runtime-dir path is an accepted residual, on the operator's word.

The strict-modes, home-tree and stamp-writer rows of the product: viola's own state handling did not move.

The session measured whether real claude on Linux loses a key typed right after a resize of its own pty, through a new KR arm of the standing live rig, and found no loss: 2.1.330 (KR) and 2.1.328 (the spare KR8-2) each kept 12 of 12 keys typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after a resize; KR8 was cut at round 8 and recorded as read, unverified.
The reading is said as no loss in 12 rounds at these delays on these versions, never as never loses; it measures the CLI unwrapped, not viola's own poll lag or the driver's paste, so no product fix was needed and no product, pty or fake-agent file changed.
The rig gained the KR arm (labels KR, KR-2, KR8, KR8-2) under the grant box,resize, its summary keys of closed words, counts, delays and settle times, and a KR-only after-key settle that counts quiet from a byte drained after the key; the shared settle of every other arm is unchanged.
The rig tells a late redraw (box clean on its re-read, the round kept, counted late-redraw) from a dirty box (still dirty on re-read, the start stops unverified).
The rehearse verb gained two rehearse-only options for the kr arm alone, a quiet window of 100 to 400 ms and a seam that withholds or delays the DEL of a round; any other arm, a malformed value, or a live start with either is refused usage, exit 2, before any ledger line.
Five KR rehearsals over the fake agent were added; nothing was retired.

decision/fake-agent-not-proof-of-real-cli: the KR rehearsals over the fake agent prove the rig's reading only; the question itself was answered by the live KR and KR8-2 starts on real claude.
decision/compat-tests-for-cli-versions and decision/multi-version-trigger-layers: the reading was taken on two CLI versions, 2.1.330 and 2.1.328, the spare kept on 2.1.328.

decision/no-sleep-synchronization, decision/no-test-retries-or-sleeps and decision/no-test-owned-real-time: KR types keys at fixed delays of 0, 20 and 100 ms after a resize and settles on a quiet window; those delays are the measurement, not synchronisation, and the settle keys on bytes read.
contract/fake-agent-receipt/size and contract/fake-agent-receipt/key: the KR rehearsals read the fake agent's size and key receipt lines to hold both sizes and each key typed.
decision/test-only-e2e-crate and decision/single-test-only-crate: every change sits in the test-only E2E crate; no product crate depends on it.
decision/pure-functions-tested-directly and decision/unit-tests-inline: the settle rule and the box word (clean, late-redraw, dirty) are pure functions held by inline rig cases.
decision/test-function-naming and decision/integration-binary-surface-prefix: the five new rehearsals are named rig_rehearsal_kr_ in the existing rig_rehearsal binary.
decision/tests-never-read-host-sessions: the KR starts keep their frames owner-only under the gitignored live-rig target dir, never read into evidence, a message or the tree.

body_fields.fact: On Linux, real claude 2.1.330 and 2.1.328 each kept 12 of 12 keys typed 0, 20 or 100 ms after a resize of their own pty: no loss in 12 rounds at these delays on these versions, never a claim that it never loses; the reading is of the CLI unwrapped, not of viola's poll lag or the driver's paste.
The KR arm's after-key settle counts its quiet window only from a byte drained after the key, never from a byte before it; every other arm keeps the shared settle unchanged.
The KR arm tells a late redraw from a dirty box: a box clean only on its re-read keeps the round and is counted late-redraw; a box still dirty on its re-read stops the start, recorded unverified.
A rehearsal of a refusal that prints none of the shared teardown words reads the refusal's own effects (no ledger, an empty receipt, no process the rig started) instead of the shared teardown check.

body: Viola's own product resize handling and wheel rules (decision/focus-mouse-resize-keep-wheel, decision/resize-baseline-is-spawn-size): the measurement resized the CLI's own pty unwrapped; no product code changed.

The driver send and paste rows (decision/paste-injection-test-layers, decision/paste-validated-at-both-ends, the driver-send and viola-send contracts): the driver-paste fix was not needed and nothing in the send path moved.
The fake agent's command line, screens, input and hook contracts: no fake-agent file changed and no fake-agent option was added.
The test harness contract, agent-run status shape, boot, cleanup and pre-push rows: no harness verb, status field or exit code changed.
CI integration, coverage floors, mutation gates, perf budgets and supply-chain rows: no workflow, gate, threshold, dependency or tool pin changed.
The MCP, wrapper channel, CLI exit-code, event-log, snapshot and log-format contracts: no product surface changed.
Test data bootstrap, test homes, fixtures and stamps: no fixture was recorded and no home, stamp or verify rule moved.
